story_text.value:
Hey everyone!

We've all loved the feeling of tuning an old radio and listening to music, commentary, or the news.

But we've mostly experienced radio as listeners. We never really got to be on the other side and have our own frequency and broadcast to others.

So I thought, what if we could combine both?

A place where anyone can have their own frequency and go live.

You can tune around, discover someone's station, or claim your own and go on air.

Please try my new puzzle game. You change the inputs in a circuit full of logic gates to try and reach the target output. I got the idea from a puzzle in a comic book. I thought it was fun and wanted to solve more of them in a less tedious manner.

I'm trying to find the sweet spot for the difficulty level and how long a daily puzzle game should take to remain fun. Hope you enjoy!

story_text.value:
Hi HN, I'm Weilun, cofounder of OpenChart.

We built OpenChart because we wanted Claude and Codex to interface with the markets, like most of humans do, through charts rather than through CLIs.

With your existing AI plans, your agent can work directly with your charts: annotate a setup, write an indicator, investigate a market move, or create an alert. The chart, conversation, and research live in the same workspace.

OpenChart alerts on any market move: draw any shape on a chart and attach an alert. When price crosses it, the alert triggers your agent to investigate the move and save the research in your workspace. The agents can work with charts, indicators, and alerts. Custom indicators and alert conditions are written in [Tea](https://github.com/longsurf-ai/tea), a programming language we built for the markets.

We believe software shouldn’t impose artificial friction on your workflow. OpenChart is built on that belief with no software cap. The source code is publicly available, and you can use free market data from day one. We also offer optional paid cloud market data for lower latency.

Everything is private. Your charts, research, and indicator code are stored on your own computer, with the app's backend running locally too.

We currently support only macOS on Apple Silicon, but we're expanding to more platforms.

Website: https://openchart.co/

Download: https://downloads.longsurf.ai/openchart/darwin/arm64/OpenCha...

We built OpenChart because we want to explore how assets can be co-manages by agents and humans. I'd especially like to hear how you are using agents to help with your investment journey.

If you like what we're building, a star on GitHub would mean a lot to us: https://github.com/longsurf-ai/openchart

story_text.value:
Hi, HackerNews!

I'm Samy, co-founder of Allchemy Labs. We built Aether, an MCP server that enables engineers to check for, understand, and fix web accessibility issues all from their IDE. Your preferred coding agent can leverage Aether to open a webpage, scan it using axe-core and return a short, prioritized list of violations along with code fixes or guidance. Every suggested fix is re-tested in a real browser before you see it, and once you apply it, your agent can re-scan the page to verify it worked. You never need to open a browser, use multiple tools, or be an expert in WCAG criteria.

Aether uses our own custom ontology architecture to provide grounded insights to any WCAG violations the scanner finds. Every WCAG technique the engine cites must pass our quality gate. Specifically, it must satisfy the violated success criterion, apply to that kind of element, and remediate that axe rule. If nothing passes, our engine will abstain rather than guess.

We compared Aether against standalone coding agent on its own (Opus 5, 30 anonymized live sites, 111 targets). While the results were mixed we have published the results especially calling out specific wins and improvement opportunities for our insight engine. Read the study here: https://allchemylabs.substack.com/p/we-tested-our-own-access...

Try Aether today, no signup needed. npx -y @allchemylabs/aether-wcag-scanner (any MCP client: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex…) Claude Code plugin: /plugin marketplace add https://github.com/allchemylabs/claude-plugins.git then /plugin install aether-wcag-scanner@allchemylabs Without a key you get the browser scan, local template fixes and verification. A free beta key adds the cloud engine: https://beta.allchemylabs.ai/?src=hn

Feedback from people who have used accessibility scanners and/or suggestion engines would be highly valuable to us, as we aim to build a tool that solves real problems and makes people's lives easier.

Happy to answer any questions and hope to hear from you.

Note: Right now Aether only checks WCAG 2.1 AA. Sites behind bot protection (e.g. Cloudflare challenges) return a "blocked" result instead of a fake scan, so point it at localhost or staging.

story_text.value:
Hi HN! Emad here, one of Octri's founders!

I think a lot of us had a similar experience as software engineers, we build API's with great features then comes the annoying part of maintaining Docs and SDKs (if any). That by itself is a lot of work without mentioning what happens if you had multiple SDKs and have to publish updates on all the different package managers!

I personally experienced that pain and was looking for solutions but most of them (if not all) are extremely expensive for an Indie, OSS, or even a startup and they actually aim for enterprise only where the big buck lives. So I decided to build all the tool that an API would need and make it available for everyone not only enterprises.

Today, I would like to present Octri.dev, a little orange octupus that takes your API spec and generates a fully customizable docs site, SDKs in 10 languages (TypeScript, Python, Dart, Rust, Swift, PHP, Ruby, Java, Kotlin, Go), and gives you an MCP server as well so agents can interact easily with your API.

I also added a new feature to the mix which is turned off by default and not included in your SDK unless you (the API owner) turn it on, it's the monitoring part that reports errors that happen for your SDK users back to you before they flood you with complaints and it pin points exactly where the issue happens. It's quite complicated to explain it in a short post so here's a page explaining it in detail: https://octri.dev/monitoring (Happy to answer any detailed questions you have regarding this below)

We also are offering a free-tier for our indie community + we have an OSS program that gives Business tier completely for free to help our great open-source community! More about the program here: https://octri.dev/open-source

We also have a free spec auditor (no sign up needed and it doesn't save your spec either): https://octri.dev/openapi-audit

Glad to have this finally out and would appreciate you guys going in and testing it out and sharing your feedback and questions below!

My email (if any needs it): emad@octri.dev

title.value: Show HN: Octri.dev – Generate customizable docs, 10 SDKs, and get an MCP server
